record.paper_title: Finiteness and periodicity of beta expansions – number theoretical and dynamical open problems
record.original_question: Let tau be an irreducible Pisot substitution on the alphabet {0,1,...,d-1}, and consider a fixed point of tau. Does there exist a nonempty word w such that occurrences of infinite patterns of the form w x_1 w x_2 w x_3 ... are relatively dense in that fixed point, where the x_i are arbitrary words and the length condition |w x_1 w x_2 ... w x_m| = |tau^{m-1}(w y)| is satisfied for some fixed word y?

evidence.quote: Let τ be an irreducible Pisot substitution on {0, 1, . . . , d − 1}.
Problem 10. In the fixed point of τ , is there a non empty word w and a relatively dense occurrences of patterns (of infinite size) of the form: wx1wx2wx3 . . .
where xi are arbitrary words satisfying |wx1wx2 . . . wxm| = |τm−1(wy)| for some fixed y ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $d\geq 2$ and let $\tau$ be a substitution on the alphabet $\mathcal{A}=\{0,1,\dots,d-1\}$, that is, a map $\tau:\mathcal{A}\to\mathcal{A}^*$ extended to $\mathcal{A}^*$ and $\mathcal{A}^{\mathbb{N}}$ by concatenation. Assume $\tau$ is primitive (some power of its incidence matrix $M_\tau\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}^{d\times d}$ has all entries positive), and that the Perron–Frobenius eigenvalue $\beta$ of $M_\tau$ is a Pisot number whose minimal polynomial over $\mathbb{Q}$ has degree $d$ (i.e. $\tau$ is an irreducible Pisot substitution). Let $u=u_0u_1u_2\cdots\in\mathcal{A}^{\mathbb{N}}$ be a fixed point of $\tau$, so $\tau(u)=u$.

A set $S\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ is called relatively dense if there exists $R>0$ such that every interval of length $R$ in $\mathbb{N}$ meets $S$.

Determine whether there must exist a nonempty word $w\in\mathcal{A}^+$ and a fixed word $y\in\mathcal{A}^*$ such that the set of indices $n\in\mathbb{N}$ for which there is an infinite sequence of words $x_1,x_2,x_3,\ldots\in\mathcal{A}^*$ with
$$u_n u_{n+1} u_{n+2} \cdots = w\,x_1\,w\,x_2\,w\,x_3\,\cdots$$
and satisfying, for every $m\geq 1$,
$$|w x_1 w x_2 \cdots w x_m| = |\tau^{m-1}(wy)|,$$
is relatively dense in $\mathbb{N}$.
artifact.status_search_result: The Pisot substitution conjecture and related strong coincidence conjecture for irreducible Pisot substitutions remain open in general. While the Pisot conjecture has been resolved for beta-substitutions and various special cases, the general question regarding combinatorial coincidence structure in fixed points of irreducible Pisot substitutions is still considered open in the literature.

status_evidence.title: On the Pisot Substitution Conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: The Pisot substitution conjecture asserts pure discrete spectrum for substitutive dynamical systems associated with irreducible Pisot substitutions.
status_evidence.claim: General Pisot substitution conjecture remains open.

status_evidence.title: The Pisot conjecture for β-substitutions
status_evidence.snippet: We prove the Pisot conjecture in the special case of beta-substitutions.
status_evidence.claim: Only the beta-substitution case is fully resolved; general irreducible case remains open.

status_evidence.title: Yet Another Characterization of the Pisot Substitution Conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Further reformulations of the still open conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: Reformulations indicate the conjecture is still being studied as open.
